title: Polymerizable ionic buffers transform grain boundaries into ion-regulating interfaces in metal halide perovskites
content: Long-term operational instability remains a critical barrier for perovskite photovoltaics toward commercial deployment, originating largely from uncontrolled ionic migration across grain boundaries. Mobile A-site cations and halide ions transform grain boundaries in metal-halide perovskites into nanoscale ion-transport pathways, undermining device stability. Here, we develop a polymerizable imidazolium tetrafluoroborate ionic buffer that chemically stabilizes mobile A- and X-site species while physically confining grain-boundary pathways. The BF4− counterion interacts with undercoordinated Pb sites, whereas the propargyl-substituted imidazolium cation stabilizes organic A-site cations, suppresses deprotonation, and scavenges reactive iodine species. Upon post-deposition activation, the cation undergoes in situ polymerization within grain-boundary regions to form an amorphous intergranular network. Correlative nanoscale characterization reveals reduced ion redistribution, electrostatic heterogeneity, and local electrical hysteresis. The inverted perovskite solar cells reach 27.25% efficiency (certified 27.03%), while 13.95 cm2 modules achieve a certified 24.10% efficiency and retain 95% of their initial performance after 2000 h of continuous maximum power point tracking. Outdoor testing supports the practical viability of this grain-boundary protection strategy.
